quarterly_data.quarter: Eli Lilly press release: Lilly's EloraTZP (combination of eloralintide and (09-30-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Lilly reported positive results from a 48-week Phase 2b trial of EloraTZP, an investigational combination of eloralintide (a selective amylin receptor agonist) and tirzepatide, in 367 adults with obesity or overweight and type 2 diabetes (presented at EASD); all combinations met the primary and secondary endpoints. From an average baseline of 232.4 lbs (105.4 kg) and A1C of 8.1%, EloraTZP cut body weight by 13.2% to 23.3% (up to 54.1 lbs at Elora 9 mg + TZP 15 mg) and A1C by up to 2.9%, versus 14.8% and 2.4% with tirzepatide 15 mg alone, up to 12.3% and 1.4% with eloralintide alone, and 3.0% and 0.3% on placebo (efficacy estimand). Gastrointestinal adverse events were more frequent in the combination arms; discontinuation due to adverse events was 10.8% to 27.0% with EloraTZP, 0% to 10.8% with eloralintide, 2.9% with tirzepatide and 16.7% with placebo. Eloralintide is already in Phase 3 trials as a single agent for obesity, and Lilly plans to initiate Phase 3 studies of an EloraTZP co-formulation by the end of 2026 (Q4 2026) using an optimized escalation schedule. Kenneth Custer (EVP, president of Lilly Cardiometabolic Health) called EloraTZP 'our next frontier'.
